title: Low back pain · 34-year-old woman
summary: A 34-year-old office worker with six months of low back pain asks about acupuncture.
learningOutcomes: Screen low back pain for cauda equina and other red flags before needling
Ask about pregnancy before choosing points in a woman of reproductive age
Locate the bladder-channel and governor-vessel points of the lower back on this patient and needle them at depths that respect what lies beneath

patient.chiefComplaint: Low back pain for six months
patient.triageNote: Walked in; asks whether acupuncture could help her back.

persona.personality: Busy, organised project manager; direct and a little impatient.
persona.openingLine: Hi doctor — it's my lower back. It's been going on for months.
concerns: She worries it is a slipped disc.

phases.label: First visit
phases.description: Thursday 18:30 at the clinic, after work.

history.question: What brings you in today?
history.answer: My lower back has been aching for about six months — worse after long days at the desk. A colleague said acupuncture helped him.

history.question: How did it start, and how has it changed?
history.answer: It started gradually during a stressful project with lots of overtime. No injury that I remember. It's been about the same since.

history.question: Where exactly is the pain?
history.answer: Across the lower back, a bit more on the right side.

history.question: Does the pain go down your leg — any numbness or tingling?
history.answer: No, it stays in the back. No numbness or pins and needles.

history.question: What makes it worse or better?
history.answer: Sitting for more than an hour and bending make it worse. Walking around and a hot shower help. It's stiff for ten minutes in the morning.

history.question: Any numbness around your groin or bottom, or trouble passing urine or opening your bowels?
history.answer: No, nothing like that.

history.question: Any fever, weight loss, pain at night, or a history of cancer?
history.answer: No fever, my weight is stable, no cancer. The pain doesn't wake me.

history.question: Any weakness in your legs?
history.answer: No.

history.question: Is there any chance you could be pregnant?
history.answer: No, I'm not pregnant.

history.question: What other medical conditions do you have?
history.answer: Nothing really — mild eczema.

history.question: What medicines do you take — including blood thinners or supplements?
history.answer: Just ibuprofen now and then when the back is bad. No blood thinners.

history.question: Do you bruise or bleed easily?
history.answer: No.

history.question: What treatment have you had so far?
history.answer: My GP said it's muscular and gave me painkillers. I've tried some stretching videos.

history.question: Have you had acupuncture before? How do you feel about needles?
history.answer: Never had it. Needles are fine — I donate blood.

history.question: What is your work like?
history.answer: Desk job, ten-hour days, a lot of stress at the moment.

history.question: What worries you, and what would you like to get back to?
history.answer: I'm worried it's a slipped disc. I'd like to play badminton again.

history.question: Does warmth help? Do you feel tired or cold?
history.answer: A hot shower helps. I get tired easily lately, and by evening my lower back feels weak and sore.

history.question: How are your sleep, appetite, bowels and periods?
history.answer: I sleep badly when work is stressful. Appetite, bowels and periods are normal.

history.question: How has your back been since the treatment?
history.answer: Better — I can sit through meetings with less pain, about three out of ten now.

history.question: Any new problems since last time — numbness, bladder or bowel changes?
history.answer: No, nothing new.

exam.finding: Normal posture; no deformity; skin intact over the lower back.

exam.maneuver: Palpate the lumbar spine and paraspinal muscles
exam.finding: No midline bony tenderness. Tight, tender right paraspinal muscles, maximal at one point at the level of L4/5.
Flexion mildly limited by pain; extension and side flexion full.

exam.maneuver: Examine leg power, reflexes and sensation, including the saddle area
exam.finding: Normal power, reflexes and sensation in both legs; saddle sensation normal.
Slightly purple tongue with a thin white coat.

exam.maneuver: Feel the radial pulses (TCM pulse diagnosis)

exam.finding: Right paraspinal tenderness much reduced; full lumbar flexion.

examNotRecorded: Nothing remarkable is recorded for that examination in this case.

objectives.title: Take a focused history, including red flags and pregnancy
objectives.hint: Onset, radiation, cauda equina symptoms, fever, weight loss, night pain, pregnancy, medicines.

objectives.title: Examine the back and the legs
objectives.hint: Palpate the spine and muscles; check leg power, reflexes and sensation including the saddle area.

objectives.title: Close the encounter safely
objectives.hint: Every needle accounted for, the record written, follow-up arranged.

rubric.text: Asked about saddle numbness and bladder or bowel change

debrief.title: Low back pain in a 34-year-old woman
debrief.conclusion: Chronic non-specific low back pain without red flags. Acupuncture can be discussed with the conflicting guideline positions made clear (NICE NG59 against; ACP 2017 among first-line non-drug options).
keyReasoning: No radiation, normal neurology and no cauda equina symptoms.
Not pregnant: the usual point cautions do not apply.
teachingPoints: Always screen for cauda equina symptoms.
Ask about pregnancy before needling a woman of reproductive age.
The kidneys and the dural sac lie deep to the lumbar points: needle depth follows this patient's build.
